dissent: Finite precharge is correctly implemented: charge.take(1) precedes every inspected prefix including prefix 0, exhaustion propagates deliberately, and audited_prefixes counts only completed prefixes.

The stale/retained ordering (prior bypass before boundary-stale; wrong-caller before prior; duplicate only on canonical equality) and receipt-identity/parent-lineage checks accurately match guard_a/guard_b/guard_audit and q_audit; the 'unproved' status when no case enters the retained branch is appropriately non-theorem.
No o19 control-build counterpart exists in the recovery index; absent controls are a missing prerequisite for interoperability comparison, not a defect of these bytes.
findings: _advance (~L67-83) omits bindings the frozen contract requires: literal occurrence uniqueness and per-event profile['requires'] subset, and q_profile == subprofile(profile) ('literal occurrence and outer dependency', 'fixed Q occurrence positions' in adapter_traces.restore). inspect_cases also never validates the restored prefix-0 states against the initialization predicates that check.audit_case re-runs (sc.initialization/audit.initialization). A case with forged initial state, dependency-violating event order, or wrong q_profile passes self-consistently. Minimal fix: enforce initialization on initial states and add occurrence/requires/subprofile checks. Additionally ValueError from .index() inside _advance escapes the except (KeyError,TypeError,IndexError,_Corrupt) boundary, aborting the whole audit instead of recording a violation.

No source-adapter correspondence is ever checked. Each pub prefix validates each side against its own view only; the checker never requires s_now['decision']==a_now['decision'], journal EXTRA-field equality with the source ledger, or consistency with the retained row's responses_related/differing_journal_fields (adapter_traces.comparison/response). A case whose adapter journal attestation/staged_source diverges from the source can be locally valid on both sides yet corrupt; undetected. Fix: per prefix compare decisions and journal-vs-source EXTRA fields, or verify the retained row relation fields.

In _transition (~L138), `same` is true only for pub-retry and identical-staged pub-commit; pub-rival with a prior receipt is hardcoded to E-IDEMPOTENCY-CONFLICT. But q_domain.incoming rebuilds the rival envelope deterministically from current staged, and q_audit/s_inclusive decide duplicate vs conflict by canonical envelope equality. Fixture: a profile containing pub-rival@i ... pub-rival@j with staged untouched between reconstructs an identical envelope, so Q returns 'duplicate' while the checker demands conflict -> false counterexample on a legitimate history. Fix: compute `same` by comparing the reconstructed incoming envelope to prior[0] for every pub verb.

Per-branch preservation sets are incomplete. The duplicate branch checks reply/receipts/revision/reads/selected but omits publication_store, staged and cut_delivery (a store-dropping or staged-mutating 'duplicate' passes). The fresh-commit branch requires only store membership, not exact append (an old store row may be dropped; uncleared cut_delivery unflagged, though q_inclusive sets cut_delivery='' on ok). The refusal branch omits staged/cut_delivery. Fix: extend each branch's equality set to all publication fields, mirroring the exact patch sets in q_inclusive/q_audit.
limitations: Static review of packet bytes only; no code was imported or executed and no run is claimed.
Line anchors are approximate, derived from the supplied byte content; original reducers were treated as reference data, not authority.
Reachability of the pub-rival counterexample shape depends on a profile containing two pub-rival occurrences; none was enumerated here.
Findings are confined to the audited fields/branches; unscoped gaps (e.g., checked_payload on store rows, source_head binding) may be intentional scope limits rather than defects.
summary: NEEDS_CORRECTION. Static re-review of hash-verified recovered bytes for o19-publication-duplicate-implement (publication_duplicate.py, sha 589b844d...). The checker faithfully mirrors the guard ordering (retained-request bypass before 'source-boundary-stale', 'wrong-caller' before duplicate/conflict), durable receipt identity/parent lineage, and per-prefix charge.take(1) precharge. However it drops several bindings the frozen restore/audit contract enforces, never compares source and adapter sides to each other, misclassifies repeated pub-rival as conflict, and leaves publication fields outside its per-branch preservation sets unchecked. No o19 control-build proposal exists in the recovery index, so checker/control interoperability could not be compared: prerequisite missing.
